candidates.term: The Alchemist inside the Year Gate
candidates.defline: The Alchemist lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your childhood was care that came in unusual forms.
candidates.reading: As a child you were loved through books or silence or an adult who cared for you in ideas more than in hugs. Because you learned early to feed your own mind, you have depended on yourself for understanding ever since. You grew up through odd subjects and unlikely teachers, at a pace nobody at home could set for you. Time alone still restores you in a way company never quite does, and you are used to being slightly apart.
candidates.teaser: Your roots hold an unusual nurture: care that came sideways, through books, silence, or an unconventional guardian. Solitude restores you, and always will.

domain_readings.Family: Nurture came to you sideways: through books, silence, an unconventional guardian, or a house where love spoke in ideas. The family remains slightly puzzled by you, lovingly. Translate yourself occasionally. They funded the library without reading it, and that too was love.
domain_readings.Mind: Your mind feeds itself and always has: self-taught in the corners, curious past every curriculum. The root gives you intellectual self-sufficiency most people never develop. Trust it. What you teach yourself stays taught, and the syllabus was always yours.
domain_readings.Growth: Growth arrives through the unusual door in every era of your life: the odd mentor, the sideways opportunity, the path nobody recommended. Keep walking through those. The conventional doors were never locked. They were just empty for someone built like you.

candidates.life_chapter: Your early chapter grew in the margins: nourishment found sideways, wisdom gathered from unassigned shelves. Those quiet roots feed everything unusual and valuable about you now. Expect your beginnings to make sense only in retrospect, and gloriously.
candidates.relations: The unconventional guardian is this seat’s person: whoever fed your mind when the standard channels missed you, a grandmother of odd wisdom, an absent parent’s bookshelf. The nurture was real and strangely shaped. Honor it by nurturing strangely too.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the margins go unread: the self-feeding mind on rations. Claim your hour of strange study daily. It is nourishment, literally.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the sideways becomes the only direction: help refused unless unusual. Accept one ordinary kindness plainly.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the root hides in its own depth: fed alone, known by none.
candidates.health_line: Your constitution is quietly particular: it thrives on routines others find austere and sickens on excess others call fun. Trust your settings.

Family.headline: You were loved at home in an unusual way.
Family.recognition: You show love to your family through ideas and help with problems more than through surface warmth. Because the care you got early was quiet and odd, you trust a relative who understands you more than one who fusses over you, and you feel lonely at noisy gatherings. You come home as the quiet one, and your relatives have stopped trying to change that.
Family.lived: In your first home someone gave you books, questions or long silences in place of the usual fuss, often an adult who lived in their own head. By your teens you had learned to answer your own questions, and you asked for help less than other children did.

Mind.headline: You taught yourself most of what you know.
Mind.recognition: You learn best alone, from books and odd sources and your own testing, at a pace no class has ever matched. Because nobody handed you a set path, you trust the understanding you dig out yourself, and you forget what you were simply told. You know a great deal that you have never shown anyone.
Mind.lived: Whatever you were given to read when you were small, you read past it into subjects nobody around you shared. By your teens you knew more about a few odd things than most adults did, and you mentioned it only to the one or two people who asked.

Growth.headline: Your growth comes through the unusual teacher.
Growth.recognition: You grow fastest through unusual people and unplanned turns, the odd teacher or the subject you stumbled on. Because the standard routes never fitted how you learn, you find them dull and leave them early. You grow in your own order, and others notice only when it is done.
Growth.lived: A person outside the usual line taught you most as a child, a neighbour or relative with odd interests who took you seriously. By your teens you had grown in ways your family could not quite follow, and you had stopped expecting them to.
